name: Light Lime
lede: Light Lime is a pale yellow-green built by adding the modifier light to lime, recorded in both the 1955 ISCC-NBS system and the 2010 xkcd color survey.

sections.title: A light build of lime
sections.body:
The nearest named colors on file are [[light-pea-green]], [[kiwi]], [[inchworm]] and [[celery]], at 3.2, 4.2, 4.2 and 5.2 ΔE [1]. It is recorded in the ISCC-NBS system of 1955, which gives it as block 131 and again as block 116, and separately in the xkcd color survey of 2010 [1]. In Munsell notation it sits at 7.7GY 9.1/12.5, and in LCH at lightness 92, chroma 77, hue 128 degrees, a bright, high-lightness green-yellow [1]. 

The library records four near-duplicate names within a few units of this swatch: Pale Lime, Light Grass Green, Light Lime Green and Pale Lime Green, the closest only 1.1 units off [2]. That crowding is typical of a modifier name: many surveyed speakers reach for slightly different words to describe the same light yellow-green. Light Lime has no separate history of its own beyond the systems that recorded it; see [[lime]] for the base color's longer record.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive has a color within CIEDE2000 4 of Light Lime covering even 1% of its canvas, as photographed [3]. That describes this archive, not painting as a whole, and a near miss is likely hiding in paintings our color match does not catch [3].
